title: Peninsula
concept: Opposing land tongues project into open water, creating defensible necks, long exposed shores and lateral landing options.
difference: Unlike straits, the central contest is over broad land heads and their necks, while a continuous open-water route remains around both sides.
routes: Ground forces hold or push through each peninsula neck toward the opposing head.
Ships retain a deep-water crossing through the central gap and can threaten the exposed sides.
Amphibious forces can land along the long outer coasts and bypass a defended neck.
economy: Mirrored home resources secure the bases; expansion metal is shared across peninsula heads and the surrounding water.
core_wishes: Registry and watermark assignment by the core integration owner.
